quarterly_data.quarter: Sanofi Bank of America healthcare conference 2026 (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CSO Mike Quigley: new head of R&D Paulo ('Paul'), who joined three weeks earlier, is leading an additional rigorous assessment of the late-stage development portfolio after the terminations of amlitelimab, itepekimab and belantamab; key Phase III start decisions were not put on hold but were given to him to weigh in on, which began 'as of last week' for many mid-to-late-stage programs. Outcomes are not determined - whether there is pruning or a reassessment of capital allocation 'will play out'. Sanofi is committed to 'an evolving communication' rather than a single snapshot; Quigley pointed to Q3 earnings in October as the next opportunity to update on decisions and future-looking ambitions. Other dated items he gave: PD-1/IL-15 colorectal cancer data to be presented at ESMO; the AATD asset (Q3-week regimen vs weekly plasma-derived AAT; rendered 'duvakitug alfa' in the transcript) is tracking to a U.S. filing by the end of this year on the assumption of accelerated approval, with a Phase III required for a European filing and 'no safety findings to date' in phase II; riliprubart VITALIZE still on track to read out in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 earnings in October; AATD U.S. filing tracking to end of this year; VITALIZE readout 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Sanofi Bank of America healthcare conference 2026 (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CSO Mike Quigley on business development: BD now sits along with M&A and Sanofi Ventures under the CFO, with R&D diligence signing off first; a year to 18 months ago the focus was 'squarely on bolt-on phase I, phase II assets', while today Sanofi is 'certainly phase agnostic' within its core I&I, rare disease and vaccines focus, with near-term opportunities adjacent to its rare and I&I (dermatology, respiratory) expertise; 'we will never move simply because of time and sense of urgency'. He targets a nominally 50/50 split of internal versus external innovation in research and early development, said first-in-human starts over the last couple of years 'have been, quite honestly, abysmal' and will build back from 2026 into 2027 and 2028, and said Sanofi will announce more platform-sized research partnerships. Research cycle: anything started today reaches the clinic in on average 4+ years and the market in 14 years in a success scenario.
quarterly_data.figure: 50/50 internal vs external innovation; 4+ years to clinic, 14 years to market

quarterly_data.quarter: Sanofi Bank of America healthcare conference 2026 (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CSO Mike Quigley on the Regeneron alliance: early conversations cover what could go into the alliance in dermatology, respiratory and 'a slight opportunity' in gastroenterology (the EoE indication only). A prototypical Sanofi asset that could be brought in is lunsekimab (TSLP/IL-13 nanobody, respiratory), not yet decided; Sanofi is also 'digging into' Regeneron's long-acting IL-13, and the TNF/OX40L bispecific (rendered 'revekimab' in the transcript) does not sit within the conversation. Whether IL-4 receptor is in or out of the alliance is part of 'ongoing negotiations and clarifications'; bringing external assets into the collaboration is 'certainly in scope'.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sanofi Bank of America healthcare conference 2026 (09-22-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CSO Mike Quigley on pipeline: frexalimab - ongoing conversations with regulators globally to adjust the primary readout from superiority to non-inferiority versus teriflunomide, with ARR still the primary endpoint and six-month disability progression the key secondary; the target is at least CD20-level ARR with a disability-progression benefit. STAT6: two programs in the clinic, an SH2 domain inhibitor with partner Recludix (Recludix responsible for early clinical development) and a degrader with partner Nurix (Sanofi responsible for clinical development); no material data release guided between now and 2028. Ophthalmology: two gene therapy programs, one in phase II in neovascular AMD and one moving into phase II in geographic atrophy. The Translate Bio mRNA platform is being used, with other lipid nanoparticle platforms and Sanofi's nanobody technology, for in vivo CAR T efforts that will emerge in the early clinical pipeline.
quarterly_data.figure: two STAT6 programs in the clinic; no material data guided before 2028; two ophthalmology gene therapy programs
